---

## What is ConnectOnion?

ConnectOnion is the open-source Agent CLI harness (`co`) and Python AI agent framework. Current stable version: 1.9.6. License: Apache-2.0.

One command line, `co`, gives Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or your own Python agent direct, progressive-disclosure access to Gmail, Outlook, Google Calendar, OneNote, Obsidian, a real logged-in Chrome browser (`co browser`), WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Feishu/Lark, Microsoft Teams, SMS, Google Drive, Linear, Canny, Synology NAS, and local source-linked Markdown memory (`co rem`). Agents discover tools on demand via `--help` without MCP schema bloat in the system prompt. ConnectOnion also ships a Python SDK (`from connectonion import Agent, llm_do, xray`) where plain Python functions become tools automatically.

**Core facts:**
- Install: `pip install connectonion`
- CLI entrypoint: `co` (`co init`, `co commands`, `co <service> --help`)
- License: Apache-2.0
- Minimum Python version: 3.11 (`Python >= 3.11`)
- Current channels: stable `1.9.6`; opt-in preview `1.9.7rc30` (previews require an exact version pin)
- Default model: `co/gemini-3.7-flash` (managed keys via `co init` / `co auth` include $5 credit, or bring your own OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / Ollama API keys)
- Starting point: `co init` gives your agent a `0x` address, mailbox, and `$5` credit; `co create my-agent` scaffolds a working Python agent project
- GitHub: https://github.com/openonion/connectonion
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/connectonion/
- Docs: https://docs.connectonion.com
- Discord: https://discord.gg/4xfD9k8AUF

**Philosophy:** "Keep simple things simple, make complicated things possible."

---

## Installation

```bash
pip install connectonion
co init    # Create agent identity, mailbox, and managed keys ($5 free credits)
```

Normal `pip install connectonion` installs the stable channel (`1.9.6`) and ignores alpha, beta, and RC releases. To test an opt-in preview, pin its exact version: `python -m pip install --upgrade 'connectonion==1.9.7rc30'`.

---

## Agent CLI Harness (`co`) & Local Memory (`co rem`)

ConnectOnion's `co` CLI harness connects any coding or custom AI agent to real-world tools with progressive disclosure (`--help` costs zero tokens until invoked, and write commands preview effects until `--yes`):

- **Mail, Calendar & Notes:** `co email` (the agent's own `0x...@mail.openonion.ai` mailbox with zero DNS setup), `co gmail`, `co outlook`, `co gcalendar`, `co onenote`
- **Persistent Logged-in Browser:** `co browser` drives one real Chrome profile across commands without writing Playwright scripts or repeating 2FA logins
- **Chat Apps as File Inboxes:** `co whatsapp`, `co telegram`, `co discord`, `co slack`, `co feishu`, `co sms`
- **Files, Search & Ops:** `co gdrive`, `co syno` (Synology NAS), `co search`, `co server`, `co schedule`, `co proxy`, `co handoff`
- **Coding Agent Integration & Auditing:** `co skills link` wires ConnectOnion skills into Claude Code and Codex; `co audit` scores any CLI's `--help` pages for agent legibility; `co benchmark` evaluates skills
- **Local Context Memory (`co rem`):** Builds and maintains a local, source-linked Markdown notebook (`~/.co/rem`) with a knowledge graph, privacy curtains, and a live reader across mail, chats, and coding sessions (`https://docs.connectonion.com/rem`, `https://docs.connectonion.com/cli/rem`)

---

## Release Strategy & OIP Protocol

ConnectOnion treats a version as a compatibility promise. Stable `1.9.6` is the default production channel; opt-in `1.9.7rc*` release candidates carry upcoming work under an exact version pin. Normal `pip install` upgrades never install previews.

OIP 0.1 is the first-party browser protocol. The Python Host serves authenticated `/ws`, `@connectonion/react` owns browser connection and event state, and O Chat renders it. Codex and Claude Code remain native backend adapters that preserve provider sessions and translate bounded activity into OIP tool events.

- Design decision: https://docs.connectonion.com/blog/oip-native-coding-adapters — one OIP browser lifecycle, native coding adapters, deterministic Codex routing, and open-without-turn Work Rooms
- Release channels: https://docs.connectonion.com/releases

---

## Design Decision: Work Room Is a Remote Client

Work Room remotely controls one native Codex or Claude Code session on the
user-owned Host. It keeps attributed user/provider conversation, authoritative
lifecycle, current work, provider controls, and a fixed provider-targeted
composer inside one shared shell. Approval, Stop, reconnect, provider-busy,
terminal, and older-client states can disable input with an explicit summary;
they do not remove the conversation or composer.

Core remains the only writer of provider authority, React validates the typed
OIP projection, and O Chat renders the client. Provider-specific controls stay
separate when a generic permission enum would lose native meaning.

Outer COAI permission is the Host ceiling, not the Codex or Claude Code
profile. The Work Room renders a finite provider-native catalog bound to one
authoritative revision. Codex Ask for approval and Approve for me keep their
different reviewers even though both use `:workspace`; Claude Code retains its
own native profile IDs. A selection becomes visible only after Host verifies
owner, Operator role, revision, ceiling, and any separate elevated-risk
confirmation.

- Design journal: https://docs.connectonion.com/blog/workroom-is-a-view
- Markdown source: https://docs.connectonion.com/tutorials/workroom-is-a-view.md
- O Chat contract: https://github.com/openonion/oo-chat/issues/210

---

## Design Decision: The Owner Needs a Door

The careful `co ai` default must keep strangers out without locking out the
person who started it. ConnectOnion 1.6.8 creates one private owner invite when
the global identity has none, preserves it across restarts, serializes
simultaneous first starts, and stores it in the owner credential file. Normal
startup and `co keys` output never reveal the value; `co keys --reveal` is the
explicit private disclosure path.

- Design journal: https://docs.connectonion.com/blog/the-owner-needs-a-door
- CLI guide: https://docs.connectonion.com/cli/ai

---

## Release Decision: One Fix, Every Newer Line

Every stable patch now links a separate open issue labelled
`forward-port-required`. The tracker names every active higher line and stays
open until each applicable focused PR merges and passes CI. While any tracker
remains open, the protected workflow refuses to publish a newer preview, RC, or
next-minor Stable. Product fixes, tests, migrations, documentation, and
operational contracts move forward; stable version/channel metadata does not.

- Policy journal: https://docs.connectonion.com/blog/a-patch-must-move-forward
- Markdown source: https://docs.connectonion.com/tutorials/a-patch-must-move-forward.md

## Reliability Decision: Text Must Prove It Is an Image

The formatter strictly decodes candidate base64 and verifies a complete PNG,
JPEG, GIF, or WebP before uploading. Truncated data URLs and decodable non-image
text remain ordinary tool output, while genuine upload failures stay loud.

- Design journal: https://docs.connectonion.com/blog/an-image-prefix-is-not-an-image
- Markdown source: https://docs.connectonion.com/tutorials/an-image-prefix-is-not-an-image.md

## Permission Decision: Headless Still Has an Operator

Unattended Auto honors deliberate operator command rules for ordinary commands.
The shipped broad `Bash(co *)` compatibility rule restores `co status` and
`co browser ...`, but does not silently authorize deployment, publication,
email, credentials, or unknown effects.

- Design journal: https://docs.connectonion.com/blog/headless-does-not-mean-unconfigured
- Markdown source: https://docs.connectonion.com/tutorials/headless-does-not-mean-unconfigured.md

ConnectOnion 1.6.12 adds explicit server-region selection, scoped mailbox
sharing, collision-safe Outlook downloads that skip inline signature images,
and explicit network bounds for every provider client. Applicable fixes are
forward-ported into the stabilising 1.7 line and `main`/1.8 with focused tests.
Release-only version metadata is never copied forward. After 1.7 Stable is
verified, its release branch is merged back into `main` so a supported newer
line cannot silently lose a Stable fix.

- Release journal: https://docs.connectonion.com/blog/connectonion-1-6-12
- Markdown source: https://docs.connectonion.com/tutorials/connectonion-1-6-12.md
- Propagation issue: https://github.com/openonion/connectonion/issues/1265

---

## Design Decision: A Page Should Not Become a Wall

Received and sent mail now share a 1,000-row page ceiling, and received mail
accepts an offset through the backend, Python tool, skill, and CLI. The client
does not silently clamp oversized requests, equal timestamps have a stable
message-ID tie-breaker, and a full CLI page prints the exact next-page command.
Finite pages protect the service without making older mail unreachable.

- Design journal: https://docs.connectonion.com/blog/a-page-should-not-become-a-wall
- CLI guide: https://docs.connectonion.com/cli/email

---

## Minimal Agent (2 lines)

```python
from connectonion import Agent

agent = Agent("assistant", tools=[my_function])
result = agent.input("Do the task")
```

Any Python function with type hints and a docstring becomes a tool automatically.

---

## Agent Class — Full API

```python
Agent(
    name="my_bot",                     # Required: agent identifier
    tools=[func1, func2],              # Optional: Python functions as tools
    system_prompt="You are helpful",   # Optional: string, file path, or Path object
    model="co/gemini-3.7-flash",       # Optional: LLM model (default: co/gemini-3.7-flash)
    max_iterations=10,                 # Optional: max tool call loops
    api_key="sk-...",                  # Optional: override env variable
    plugins=[skills, tool_approval],   # Optional: plugin list
    log=True,                          # Optional: logging (True/False/path)
    quiet=False,                       # Optional: suppress console output
    trust="open",                      # Optional: security trust level
)
```

**Methods:**
- `agent.input("task")` — run agent on a task, returns final response string
- `agent.input("task", max_iterations=20)` — override iterations per call
- `agent.add_tool(fn)` — add a tool after creation
- `agent.remove_tool("name")` — remove a tool
- `agent.list_tools()` — list registered tools

---

## Tool System

Any Python function with type hints and docstring becomes a tool:

```python
def search_web(query: str, max_results: int = 5) -> str:
    """Search the web for information.

    Args:
        query: The search query
        max_results: Maximum number of results to return

    Returns:
        Search results as formatted text
    """
    # ... implementation
    return results

agent = Agent("researcher", tools=[search_web])
```

ConnectOnion reads `query: str` → schema type string, `max_results: int = 5` → optional integer with default, docstring → tool description. No decorators needed.

**Copy built-in tools:**
```bash
co copy gmail         # → tools/gmail.py
co copy shell         # → tools/shell.py
co copy memory        # → tools/memory.py
co copy browser_tools # → tools/browser_tools/
co copy file_tools    # → tools/file_tools/
co copy web_fetch     # → tools/web_fetch.py
```

---

## Supported Models

| Prefix | Provider | Example |
|--------|----------|---------|
| `co/` | OpenOnion managed keys | `co/gemini-3.7-flash` (default), `co/gemini-2.5-pro`, `co/gpt-4o` |
| `gpt-*` | OpenAI (bring your own key) | `gpt-4o`, `gpt-4o-mini` |
| `claude-*` | Anthropic (bring your own key) | `claude-sonnet-4-5` |
| `gemini-*` | Google (bring your own key) | `gemini-2.5-pro` |

**co/ managed keys:** No API key needed. New accounts get $5 free credits. Initialize with `co init` or `co auth`.

```python
agent = Agent("bot", model="co/gemini-3.7-flash")   # default managed key
agent = Agent("bot", model="gpt-4o")                # your OpenAI key
agent = Agent("bot", model="claude-sonnet-4-5")     # your Anthropic key
```

---

## Event System — 12 Lifecycle Hooks

```python
from connectonion import Agent, after_user_input, before_llm, after_llm
from connectonion import before_tools, after_tools, before_each_tool, after_each_tool
from connectonion import on_error, on_complete, on_stop_signal, on_agent_ready

@after_user_input
def log_input(agent):
    print(f"User: {agent.current_session['messages'][-1]['content']}")

@after_tools
def log_tools(agent):
    print(f"Tools called this iteration: {len(agent.current_session['trace'])}")

agent = Agent("bot", tools=[fn], on_events=[log_input, log_tools])
```

**Available hooks (in execution order):**
1. `on_agent_ready` — fired once when agent initializes
2. `after_user_input` — after user message added, before LLM call
3. `before_llm` — just before each LLM API call
4. `after_llm` — after LLM responds, before tool execution
5. `before_tools` — before tool batch executes (once per iteration)
6. `before_each_tool` — before each individual tool call
7. `after_each_tool` — after each individual tool call
8. `after_tools` — after tool batch completes (once per iteration)
9. `on_error` — when a tool raises an exception
10. `on_complete` — after agent finishes (last iteration or no more tools)
11. `on_stop_signal` — when agent receives stop signal

---

## Plugin System

Plugins are lists of event handlers bundled together:

```python
from connectonion import Agent
from connectonion.useful_plugins import skills, tool_approval, re_act

agent = Agent("assistant", tools=[bash, file_tools], plugins=[skills, tool_approval])
```

**Built-in plugins:**

| Plugin | Import | Purpose |
|--------|--------|---------|
| `skills` | `from connectonion.useful_plugins import skills` | /slash command invocation with scoped permissions |
| `tool_approval` | `from connectonion.useful_plugins import tool_approval` | Web UI for approving dangerous tool calls |
| `re_act` | `from connectonion.useful_plugins import re_act` | ReAct reasoning: plan before action, reflect after |
| `eval` | `from connectonion.useful_plugins import eval` | Judge if task is complete |
| `subagents` | `from connectonion.useful_plugins import subagents` | Spawn parallel sub-agents |
| `auto_compact` | `from connectonion.useful_plugins import auto_compact` | Compress context at 90% capacity |
| `system_reminder` | `from connectonion.useful_plugins import system_reminder` | Inject guidance after tool results |
| `ulw` | `from connectonion.useful_plugins import ulw` | Ultra Light Work: fully autonomous continuous mode |
| `ui_stream` | `from connectonion.useful_plugins import ui_stream` | Stream agent events to WebSocket UI |
| `image_result_formatter` | `from connectonion.useful_plugins import image_result_formatter` | Format base64 images for vision models |
| `shell_approval` | `from connectonion.useful_plugins import shell_approval` | CLI approval prompts for shell commands |
| `gmail_plugin` | `from connectonion.useful_plugins import gmail_plugin` | Gmail OAuth setup flow |
| `calendar_plugin` | `from connectonion.useful_plugins import calendar_plugin` | Google Calendar OAuth setup |

**Copy any plugin:**
```bash
co copy re_act         # → plugins/re_act.py
co copy tool_approval  # → plugins/tool_approval.py
co copy subagents      # → plugins/subagents.py
```

---

## Skills System

Skills are markdown files invoked with `/skill-name`. They define instructions + auto-approved tool permissions.

**Discovery order (highest to lowest priority):**
1. `.co/skills/skill-name/SKILL.md` — project-level
2. `~/.co/skills/skill-name/SKILL.md` — user-level
3. `~/.claude/skills/skill-name/SKILL.md` — Claude Code compatible
4. Built-in skills shipped with ConnectOnion

**SKILL.md format:**
```yaml
---
name: commit
description: Create git commits with good messages
tools:
  - Bash(git status)
  - Bash(git diff *)
  - Bash(git add *)
  - Bash(git commit *)
  - read_file
  - glob
---

# Git Commit Skill

Step 1: Run `git status` and `git diff --staged` in parallel
Step 2: Analyze what changed and why
Step 3: Write concise commit message (under 50 chars, focus on "why")
Step 4: Commit with HEREDOC format to preserve newlines
```

**Built-in skills (copy to your project):**
```bash
co copy ship-feature  # → .co/skills/ship-feature/SKILL.md
```

`ship-feature` skill: ships a feature end-to-end — updates tests, docs/, docs-site, bumps version, tags, pushes, and publishes to PyPI.

**Claude Code compatibility:** ConnectOnion skills use the same SKILL.md format as Claude Code. Symlink useful_skills/ into ~/.claude/skills/ with `link-to-claude.sh`.

**Permission patterns:**
- `Bash(git status)` — exact command match only
- `Bash(git diff *)` — wildcard: any `git diff` variant
- `Bash(git *)` — all git commands
- `read_file` — tool name only (any arguments)

---

## llm_do() — One-shot LLM Calls

For single LLM calls without an agent:

```python
from connectonion import llm_do

# Simple call
result = llm_do("Summarize this text", model="co/gemini-3.7-flash")

# Structured output
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Sentiment(BaseModel):
    label: str  # positive, negative, neutral
    score: float  # 0.0 to 1.0

result = llm_do(
    "Analyze sentiment: 'I love this product!'",
    output_type=Sentiment,
    model="co/gemini-3.7-flash"
)
# result.label == "positive", result.score == 0.95
```

Default model for `Agent` and `llm_do`: `co/gemini-3.7-flash`.

## CLI Reference

Core `co` CLI harness commands (run `co commands` or `co <cmd> --help` for full discovery):

```bash
co init                        # Create agent 0x identity, mailbox, and $5 managed credit
co create my-agent             # Scaffold a new Python agent project
co auth google                 # Connect Gmail, Google Calendar, and Google Drive
co auth microsoft              # Connect Outlook, Microsoft Calendar, OneNote, and Teams
co email                       # Read/send from the agent's own 0x...@mail.openonion.ai mailbox
co gmail / co outlook          # Read, search, draft, and send Gmail / Outlook mail
co browser                     # Drive one persistent, logged-in Chrome session
co whatsapp / co telegram      # Connect chat apps as local file inboxes
co slack / co discord / co sms # Slack, Discord, Feishu/Lark, and Android SMS inboxes
co rem                         # Local source-linked Markdown memory & live reader
co skills link                 # Link ConnectOnion skills into Claude Code and Codex
co audit <cli>                 # Score any CLI's --help pages for AI agent legibility
co doctor / co status          # Check installation health, Host status, and credit balance
co keys                        # Inspect masked agent keys and credentials
co copy --list / co copy <x>   # Copy built-in tool/plugin/skill source into your project
co ai                          # AI coding assistant and remote Work Room Host
```

## @xray Debugging

```python
from connectonion import Agent, xray

@xray
def my_tool(data: str) -> str:
    """Process data."""
    # Access runtime context
    print(f"Agent: {xray.agent.name}")
    print(f"Task: {xray.task}")
    print(f"Iteration: {xray.iteration}")
    xray.trace()  # Print visual execution flow
    return f"Processed: {data}"

agent = Agent("debugger", tools=[my_tool])
agent.auto_debug()  # Enable interactive debugging
```

---

## Memory Tool

```python
from connectonion import Agent, Memory

memory = Memory()
agent = Agent("assistant", tools=[memory])

# Agent automatically reads and writes memory
agent.input("Remember that I prefer Python over JavaScript")
agent.input("What do you know about my preferences?")
# → "You prefer Python over JavaScript"
```

Memory is stored as markdown files in `.co/memory/`.

---

## Multi-Agent Networking

```python
from connectonion import Agent, host, connect

# Agent 1: specialist
specialist = Agent("specialist", tools=[analyze])
host(specialist, port=8765)  # Make callable remotely

# Agent 2: orchestrator
remote_specialist = connect("localhost:8765")
orchestrator = Agent("orchestrator", tools=[remote_specialist])
orchestrator.input("Analyze this dataset")
```

---

## Trust System

```python
from connectonion import Agent, TrustAgent

# Open: allow all requests (development)
agent = Agent("bot", trust="open")

# Careful: whitelist + LLM verification (staging)
agent = Agent("bot", trust="careful")

# Strict: whitelist only (production)
agent = Agent("bot", trust="strict")

# Custom policy
agent = Agent("bot", trust="prompts/my-policy.md")
```

---

## ConnectOnion vs Other Frameworks

**vs LangChain:**
- ConnectOnion: 2 lines to create agent, functions auto-convert to tools
- LangChain: 30+ lines, requires Tool() wrappers, chains, and prompts
- ConnectOnion has built-in debugging (@xray), plugin system, multi-agent networking

**vs AutoGen:**
- ConnectOnion: single file, no config YAML, functions as tools
- AutoGen: YAML configuration, more complex multi-agent setup

**vs CrewAI:**
- ConnectOnion: YAGNI philosophy, minimal abstractions
- CrewAI: Role-based agents, more opinionated structure

---

## Logging

ConnectOnion logs automatically to `.co/logs/{agent_name}.log` and `.co/evals/` (YAML).

```python
Agent("bot", log=True)          # Default: log to .co/logs/
Agent("bot", log=False)         # Disable logging
Agent("bot", quiet=True)        # Log to file only, suppress console
Agent("bot", log="output.log")  # Custom log path
```

Environment variable: `CONNECTONION_LOG=path/to/log.log`

## Version History

- 1.9.6 — Current stable release: cross-platform background Host from `co init`, `model: claude-code`, `co rem` Today desk, knowledge graph & three privacy levels, `co send`/`co receive`, and local `co wechat` reader
- 1.9.0 → 1.9.5 — `co rem` source-linked Markdown memory across mail, chats, and coding sessions
- 1.8.x — Agent CLI harness (`co`), `co audit`, `co benchmark`, OneNote, Slack, web search, and `co schedule`
- 1.7.0 — OIP 0.1 Work Room, native Codex and Claude Code delegation
- 1.6.6 — `co/gemini-3.7-flash` becomes the default model for `Agent` and `llm_do`
- 0.9.0 — useful_skills/ folder, ship-feature skill, co copy skills support
- 0.5.0 → 0.8.x — Trust system, multi-agent networking, plugin architecture
- 0.1.0 → 0.4.x — Multi-model support, CLI, email tools, event system
